newsitem.title: FRANCE: French sugar co-ops buy majority stake in SFS.
newsitem.headline: French sugar co-ops buy majority stake in SFS.

text.p: A group of French sugar cooperatives has acquired the 99.4 percent stake held by Compagnie Francaise de Sucrerie (CFS) in sugar producer Societe de Fabriques de Sucre (SFS), Banque Indosuez said in a statement on Monday.

Cristal Developpement, a holding controlled by Sucrerie Distillerie d'Arcis-sur-Aube, Sucrerie Distillerie Cooperative de Corbeilles en Gatinais and Sucreries Distilleries des Hauts de France, paid around 580.1 million francs for the stake or 443.80 francs per share.
Cristal Developpement plans to launch a buyout offer for the remaining SFS shares and later withdraw the stock from listing on the over-the-counter market.
This latest transaction stems from the acquisition of CFS by Eridania-Beghin Say SA for 2.85 billion francs.

Under the term of the deal reached in June, Eridania agreed to resell 52 percent of CFS assets and sugar quotas to Generale Sucriere of the Saint-Louis group and to five sugar cooperatives by the end of the 1996/97 campaign (October/September).
CFS, France's number three sugar manufacturer, produced some 456,000 tonnes of sugar in the 1995/96 season.
